The upcoming MacBook Ultra was never going to be cheap, and beyond the all-new slim design, OLED display, and touch functionality, it also has to absorb the price pressure driven by rising memory costs. The latest report suggests its production costs could be pushed even higher.

Apple has always preferred to use multiple suppliers for components to ensure a stable display supply and secure the best pricing, and originally planned to continue this strategy with the MacBook Ultra. However, according to supply chain sources, Apple has decided to use only a single display supplier...

Apple has three display partners: Samsung, LG, and BOE. BOE has so far only supplied screens for Apple's lower-end products, while orders for higher-end displays have always been split between Samsung and LG.

The MacBook Ultra will feature Apple's most sophisticated display to date, and combining a two-stack OLED with touch functionality on the large-size panel required for a laptop is no easy feat. The latest supply chain sources indicate that Apple has decided to source the panels exclusively from Samsung.

According to The Elec, LG has consistently failed to meet Apple's required production standards.

Apple required large-size substrates for mass production, and Samsung Display responded with its 8.6-generation OLED production line. LG Display was reportedly exploring the use of its existing 6-generation production line. Although a 6-generation line can also produce laptop OLEDs, substrate efficiency and capacity are both inferior to an 8.6-generation line. With initial product volumes apparently insufficient to support two suppliers, Apple ultimately chose Samsung Display as its sole supplier.

Given the limited quantities LG can produce, the logistics complexity of a dual-supplier setup is clearly not justified. LG is not expected to supply screens for the flagship MacBook until 2029 at the earliest.

This clearly puts Samsung in a stronger position in panel price negotiations, which is expected to push up Apple's production costs. Apple is also likely to pass the additional expenses on to consumers, much as it has handled the rising cost of memory.

Given that the MacBook Ultra may carry a staggeringly high price tag, how interested are you in upgrading? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
